causes.text: The European Parliament approved legislation requiring carmakers to cut CO2 emissions from new cars by 55% by 2030 and 100% by 2035, effectively banning sales of new petrol and diesel vehicles and forcing manufacturers to accelerate investment in electric vehicles.

source_info.title: EU lawmakers endorse 2035 ban on new petrol and diesel cars

effects.text: BMW's 2023 automotive margin slipped to 9.8%, slightly below the market consensus, as the company invested heavily in electrification and spent more on research and development and manufacturing costs for electric vehicles.

source_info.title: BMW shares hit by 2023 margin disappointment, profit drop

causal_reasoning_chain.description: EU legislation mandated a 100% cut in CO2 emissions from new cars by 2035, effectively outlawing petrol and diesel vehicles and pushing carmakers toward electrification.
BMW accelerated its electric-vehicle strategy, increasing spending on research, development and manufacturing for battery-powered models to meet future emissions targets.
These higher costs reduced BMW's automotive margin to 9.8% in 2023; following the results announcement, the stock slipped about 2.7%.

rationale: The impending ban on petrol and diesel vehicles forced BMW to invest more aggressively in electric vehicles. The resulting increase in R&D and production costs compressed margins, causing a slight miss against market expectations.
counterfactual_analysis: Without the EU's strict emissions law, BMW could have maintained a more balanced portfolio, slowing the pace of EV investments and preserving its automotive margin.

adversarial_confounders.impact: Rising prices for lithium and other battery materials independently increased costs and may have contributed to margin pressure

details.pestel_factor: Economic - Semiconductor shortages disrupting global auto production
details.commentary: A fragile chip supply chain forced automakers worldwide to idle plants and prioritize high-margin models, constraining volumes and raising costs. Volkswagen's cautious guidance and the volatility in its stock reflected how this economic supply shock weighed on earnings visibility and investor confidence.
